note: Hebrew lemoshchah is best taken from mashach II "measure off", a priestly share (cf. Lev 7:35), not "anointing"; the gifts are Aaron's allotted portion.
Hebrew minchah here is the cereal offering; "meat" in 1611 meant food in general, so a modern reader wrongly hears an animal sacrifice (recurs throughout Numbers).
Hebrew shoq is the leg/thigh of the animal, not the shoulder.
